blocks.text: Quick verdict

Oxylabs is the better choice for large-scale scraping, SERP and e-commerce data collection, where its pool size, ZIP and ASN targeting, 99.95% published success rate and scraper APIs matter. Proxys.io is the better choice for low-budget fixed identities in multi-account and affiliate work, bulk IPv6, and mobile proxies with unlimited bandwidth, and its 24-hour refund window makes testing cheap. The two are rarely substitutes; many teams use both for different jobs.

Proxys.io and Oxylabs serve different needs entirely. Proxys.io rents individual IPs cheaply, from $0.13 for IPv6 to a few dollars for premium residential IPv4, with unlimited bandwidth on dedicated addresses. Oxylabs is an enterprise web-data provider with a 175M+ rotating residential pool, ISP and datacenter networks and scraper APIs. This comparison helps you decide whether your work calls for fixed identities or large-scale rotation, and what each costs.

blocks.text: Proxys.io in 2026: what you get

PROXYS.IO offers both rented static addresses and a rotating residential network. The provider reports more than 100 million ISP addresses across 195 countries, country/region/city targeting, up to 100 saved parameter sets and rotation every 2-60 minutes. Its mobile service covers 14 countries with city/carrier selection and roughly 2,000-5,000 addresses per country/carrier combination. Static IPv4 covers 24 markets. These are supplied specifications, not independently measured availability. HTTP, HTTPS and SOCKS5 are included on every plan.

Strengths: Low-entry per-address products; a provider-reported 100M+ residential network; country, region and city targeting; HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS5 included; a 24-hour refund window. Weak spots: Rotating mobile traffic pricing must be checked in the cart; residential plans have 30/60/90-day validity; published pool totals do not guarantee reachable IPs; independent target-specific performance has not been established here.
Oxylabs in 2026: what you get

Oxylabs is a Lithuanian web-data company and Bright Data's closest rival at the top of the market. It advertises a residential pool of more than 175 million IPs across 195 locations, publishes a 99.95% success rate for residential traffic, and sells seven product lines including datacenter, ISP and mobile proxies, a Web Scraper API and Web Unblocker. Onboarding is more sales-led than the mid-market providers, but self-service has expanded through 2026, including dedicated ISP proxies.

Strengths: One of the two largest residential pools available; Published 99.95% residential success rate; Strong scraper APIs that bill per result; Formal ethical-sourcing documentation for procurement. Weak spots: Expensive at low volume ($8/GB PAYG); Best rates need large monthly commitments; Residential trial goes through sales rather than self-service.
Pricing: Proxys.io vs Oxylabs

PROXYS.IO separates traffic-based plans from per-address rentals. Rotating residential starts at $1.50/GB on 30, 60 or 90-day plans, without an IP or session cap. Static monthly starting prices are IPv6 $0.13, dynamic $0.27, shared IPv4 $0.67 (up to three users), foreign individual IPv4 $1.47, Windows-fingerprint IPv4 $1.87 and premium static residential IPv4 $3.60. Dedicated mobile IPv4 with unlimited traffic on a private channel starts at $56.79/month. Rotating mobile traffic is priced by the cart slider; no single starting per-GB rate has been confirmed. HEAT_RES provides 35% off eligible residential pay-per-traffic plans. Minimum static rental is one month and the refund window is 24 hours.

Oxylabs charges $8/GB pay-as-you-go for residential traffic. Monthly plans start with Starter at $30 for 5 GB ($6/GB) and a Basic tier around $100 for 20 GB, and the rate falls to $2.50/GB on the $2,500/month Corporate plan. Mobile traffic starts at $7.50/GB.

At 10 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because Proxys.io does not publish an exact price for that volume; Oxylabs comes to about $80. At 100 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because Proxys.io and Oxylabs do not publish an exact price for that volume. Both Proxys.io and Oxylabs work on allowances that do not carry forward indefinitely, so size your plan to real monthly usage rather than buying ahead.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

PROXYS.IO reports a residential pool of 100M+ ISP addresses; this has not been independently audited. Proxys.io reports 100M+ addresses and Oxylabs lists '175M+'. In practice, what matters is how many unique IPs you get in the countries you target, which you can measure in a short trial by sending a few thousand requests and counting distinct exit addresses. For coverage, Proxys.io lists 195 residential countries, with separate mobile and static coverage countries and Oxylabs lists 195. On targeting, Proxys.io offers country, region and city for residential traffic, with city/carrier selection for mobile, while Oxylabs offers country, state, city, ZIP and ASN.
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, Proxys.io offers static per-IP proxies; rotating residential and mobile, and Oxylabs offers rotating and sticky sessions on residential and mobile. Setup works the same way on both: a single gateway endpoint, with location and session options passed as username parameters, plus IP whitelisting if you prefer not to use credentials.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: compare the exact target and traffic plan before choosing. PROXYS.IO reports a 100M+ rotating residential network across 195 countries, in addition to static rentals. Pool size alone does not establish success rate; this brief does not independently benchmark PROXYS.IO against the other provider.
SERP and rank tracking: Oxylabs. Oxylabs has the edge here. Why: its scraper API returns parsed search results. How Proxys.io compares: cheap IPv6 can handle some search tasks.

Social media and multi-account management: Proxys.io wins. The deciding factor for Proxys.io: fixed dedicated or mobile IPs per account. The limitation on the Oxylabs side: it works, but the pricing is built for volume, not a handful of accounts.

E-commerce price and stock monitoring: Oxylabs. Oxylabs has the edge here. Why: city and ZIP targeting plus parsed e-commerce endpoints. How Proxys.io compares: limited rotation for large catalog crawls.
Ad verification and geo-testing: Oxylabs wins. The deciding factor for Oxylabs: broad geo coverage with ASN targeting. The limitation on the Proxys.io side: limited geo depth.

Tight budgets: Proxys.io wins. The deciding factor for Proxys.io: cheap per-IP rentals with unlimited bandwidth. The limitation on the Oxylabs side: entry pricing is among the highest in this comparison.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. Proxys.io: 24-hour refund window instead of a trial. Oxylabs: Residential trial arranged through sales, once per customer. Verification and payment rules differ too. Proxys.io: Light; crypto accepted. Oxylabs: Business verification on larger accounts. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test Proxys.io and Oxylabs before you commit
The quickest way to choose between Proxys.io and Oxylabs is a side-by-side test on the sites and countries you actually care about:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (Proxys.io: 24-hour refund window instead of a trial; Oxylabs: residential trial arranged through sales, once per customer).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.
3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, Proxys.io comes out ahead in 2, Oxylabs in 4, and 0 are ties. That makes Oxylabs the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: Proxys.io is strongest for multi-account and affiliate work that needs fixed IPs, while Oxylabs is strongest for large scraping pipelines with steady volume. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
